about:
# QuestWordHunter

WoW quests are full of the language you actually want to learn — but they fly by. You accept, scan for the objective, and the words are gone.

QuestWordHunter keeps the quest on screen as clickable text. See a word you don't know? Click it, add a meaning, mark it **Learning**. Next time it turns up in another quest it is already coloured. After a while you have a real vocabulary list built from the game, not from a textbook.

![Quest text with clickable words](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f25b0fe-5a62-46ef-b700-5cd7f0e87d78)

![Statistics of learned words](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/75fcae0e-e5f8-4db7-9eb9-fdd002bcec7a)

## What you get

Controller support includes the map and quest-log side tabs: X / Square opens the selected quest's reader and Y / Triangle opens the library. In the library, LB/RB changes tabs and LT/RT changes pages; the D-pad selects controls, A / Cross activates them and B / Circle returns. Lists and settings use the same selection outline, and left/right adjusts a selected slider. The English panel scrolls with up/down or LB/RB. With the voice engine loaded, the reader's triggers replay and pause/resume speech. Explicit WordHunter bindings take priority. ConsolePort uses its own interface cursor and configured button hints; addon windows and side tabs are registered through its public API.

- Quest text you can click instead of retyping into a notes app
- Colours and underlines for **New**, **Learning**, **Known** and **Ignored**, so you see progress in the paragraph itself — keep both or pick one
- A meaning, a personal note, and the sentence the word came from
- Previous / Next in the word editor, on the row with Cancel and Save (also the arrow keys when no box has focus, and LB/RB on a controller), so a quest can be read word by word without the mouse
- An optional **recall check**: a word you have been learning for a day asks how well you knew it, 1 to 5, before it shows its meaning. Words that keep scoring low are **difficult**, and you can export them for a flashcard app
- A word list and simple stats — `/whw words`, `/whw stats`
- A quiet **Ready for Known** hint after five different quests and two weeks. It never promotes anything by itself
- Separate lists per language, so German and French don't mix
- Windows you can move, resize and theme — `/whw settings`
- A **controller** works too: the D-pad moves between words; the reader and editor show which buttons open, save, close or switch reading mode. Needs the game's own controller support; the full map is under Settings

Buttons stay in English. Quest text stays in the language you set in WoW.

Assign shortcuts under Options → Key Bindings → AddOns → WordHunterWoW. The reader's footer and the word editor show the current bindings and update when you change them. With controller support enabled in both WoW and the addon, hints use the client's controller button labels, including its selected Xbox/PlayStation glyphs. Explicit WordHunterWoW controller bindings override the panel's default controls. Unassigned keyboard actions have no invented default. The editor's arrow keys and recall ratings 1–5 work locally outside combat; arrows move the text caret while typing. Enter saves from the translation field, and Escape closes the windows.

## Quest library

Open `/whw quests`, or click the **WordHunterWoW book side tab** beside the Quest Log.
The library follows your learning language from Settings. The reader displays
English alongside that language when both texts are available. Words and recall
ratings are saved separately for each language.
The **German Dictionary** includes German and English Classic quest texts,
plus native Forever cache records; no separate quest-data addon is needed.
Text actually seen in your client takes
precedence, and offers are archived immediately so you can study them after a
fast party has completed the quest.
No quest needs to be selected. The library opens on **My quests**, containing
this character's current and completed quests. **Show only current quests in
quest log** hides the completed-only entries. The **All in game quests** tab
contains all quest records stored for this game client. Both tabs display English
and learning-language titles, with search in either language or by ID and pagination.
Same-title variants are collapsed into one entry. Click **variants >** to choose
another ID; its full dialogue remains independently readable. A current quest
is preferred when opening a collapsed group. The footer separates entries from
quest IDs, because the game's completion flags include multiple versions of a
quest and are not a count of distinct stories or reading sessions.
The three tabs attach to the right edge of the library: characters for **My quests**,
a book for **All in game quests**, and a quill for **Words**.
All WordHunter side-tab icons use 24 px inside their native tab frames.
**Words** shows vocabulary in the same window, with its own
search and status filters; clicking a word opens the normal editor.
The database is a text catalog, not a promise that every quest is currently
available from an NPC.

Click a quest to open its description and objectives in the normal reader. The
arrow side tab at its bottom-right edge returns to the library. Reading a catalog entry does not select it in
Blizzard's log or mark it completed.

The footer's **Offer / Progress / Completion** button cycles through stored quest
passages.
Quests with only dialogue open on their first available passage; words remain
clickable in the selected language. Imported dialogue has no audio until a
matching recording is provided.

Matching MultiLanguage quest sources supplement missing text, including German
text for completed quests, without replacing native observations. Items, spells
and NPC records are excluded from the quest library; their tooltip addons remain
separate. Imported quest text carries a source notice and can differ from the
current game. A title-only record opens for learning with an explicit note that
quest dialogue is missing. An unverified source field is not used as an objective.

The reader uses native quest-log text, a localized database when installed, or your
locally collected text. With **English Quest Panel** installed, English database
text is the fallback. If your target language is not English, this fallback is
clearly marked **read only**: it cannot add English words to your target-language
vocabulary or request a clip from a different-language voice pack. A German
dictionary includes the Classic/Forever quest corpus; some passages are missing. Audio
is available only where an installed pack has the corresponding passage.

Native descriptions and objectives read from an NPC or safely from the quest log,
plus the progress or completion dialogue actually displayed by an NPC,
are kept locally for reopening after completion, even when optional corpus
harvesting is off. Missing fields can be filled from the matching local database
without replacing native text. Previously completed quests need a saved native
text or a matching database passage; the completion list alone cannot recreate
their missing descriptions.

Completion history is stored per character. There is no upload. After updating
the addon, use `/reload` to load the new files.

## What changed in 1.22

**A new statistics window.** Four tabs — Overview, Growth, Forecast and Recall —
with figure tiles, your Known words over time and a 30-day pace projection, a
forecast of the words that are ready for Known, and your recall ratings.

**One look for every window.** The windows share the game's own stone and
parchment pieces (with a flat fallback on a client that lacks them), and each of
the five background styles has its own set. There is a natural and a vivid
colour palette, and you can change any of the five text and status colours in
**Settings → Appearance**.

**The other languages' dictionaries load only when needed.** The French, Spanish,
Italian and Portuguese packs take 24 to 54 MiB each and were all read at login.
Now only the pack for the language you are learning is. They need 1.22.6 or
newer, and they run on Retail, Classic Era and WoW Forever.

**Shortcut hints on buttons and side tabs.** They follow keyboard and controller
changes, and on Forever they show only in Gamepad Mode. On a controller they are
drawn from the same icon set the game's own prompts use, so an Xbox pad shows
A, B, X and Y instead of 1 to 4.

**Quest audio and word audio can be switched off separately.** **Settings → Quest
panel** has **Enable quest audio** and **Enable word audio**, both on by default.
Turn quest audio off if another add-on, such as Spoken, reads your quests: the
narrator window and the Play buttons go away. Word audio, the voice that says a
German word when you click it, keeps working. The word switch needs the updated
German voice engine (2.0.9) and the word voice pack.

**The word list and the statistics window no longer go through the whole
dictionary.** With the German dictionary the word list read all 143,000 entries
on every refresh and every pause in typing, about half a second for a search.
The first time you open the list after a login or `/reload`, the addon now
prepares an index in the background (about three seconds, a few milliseconds a
frame); until it is ready the list works as before, afterwards a search takes a
few hundredths of a second. The index keeps about 12 MB of memory.

**Logging in and reading a quest with a new word are lighter.** The saved text
of your words (`WordHunterWoWExport`) was rebuilt at every login and each time a
quest recorded a new word, about a tenth of a second each. It is now built once,
when you log out.

**The recall check's controller hints** sit on a row of their own, so with the
icons they no longer wrap onto the 1 to 5 buttons.

**Reading.** The word colours stay readable on the parchment, readable items such
as a journal, a letter or a book page open in the same reader as an NPC's
conversation, German quest sentences highlight better and show split-verb hints,
and with English Quest Panel the English sentence is picked by the words that
link the two even when the sentence counts differ.

**Dictionary words** can be reset to the pack's meaning from the word window.

## What changed in 1.21

The library has **My quests**, **All in game quests** and **Words** book side tabs, bilingual titles,
and a current-log checkbox. Completed quests use matching German source text
when available, opening the same learning reader as native quests. Returning to
the library preserves its tab, search and page. Items, spells and NPCs no longer
appear among quests.

## What changed in 1.20

**The settings have a window of their own.** `/whw settings` opens it: seven
tabs, a live preview of the quest panel that changes as you move a control, and
a **Reset this tab** button on each tab. It opens in combat too, and
`/whw settings learning` goes straight to a tab. Options → AddOns has a button
that opens the same window. Your settings are unchanged, except one: **Frame
opacity** now fades the background behind the text as well, so it starts at
100% again.

## What changed in 1.18

**A Learning word can ask before it tells.** Switch on the recall check in
`/whw settings` and a word that has been Learning for a day no longer opens
with its meaning filled in. It shows the sentence it sits in and five buttons,
1 to 5 -- no idea, to knew it at once -- and the meaning only after you have
answered, or pressed **Show meaning** to look without answering. The number
keys work too. Each word is asked at most once a day, and only when clicked in
a quest: the word list shows the meaning beside the word already, so it never
asks. The verdict is written the moment you give it; Cancel does not lose it.
Off by default, because it changes what a click does.

**Difficult words, and a way to get them out.** Five or more ratings with an
average below 3 make a word difficult. The settings page counts them and has
an **Export difficult words** button that puts them in a box you copy out of,
one word per line, tab-separated: word, meaning, note, the example sentences,
the recent average and the number of ratings. Paste it into Anki or any
flashcard program that reads a tab-separated file. `/whw difficult` says how
many there are and `/whw difficult export` opens the same box.

**The sentences come along.** Up to five example sentences are kept for every
word you mark Learning: the one it was marked in, and the ones it was met or
rated in later. They go into the export beside the word.

The ratings and sentences are stored beside your word list, not in it, so the
file the desktop Word Hunter imports is unchanged.

## Reader controls in 1.20.7

The **WordHunterWoW - Reader** book tab opens and closes Reader. In the quest
log it sits below **QUESTS**; NPC quest and dialogue windows have their own
Reader tab. Reader stays closed until clicked by default.

In `/whw settings`, **Quest panel** has separate switches for opening Reader
automatically from the quest log or when talking to NPCs. **Automatically read
quests when Reader opens** controls narration separately; when off, the narrator
appears ready and waits for Play. A closed Reader does not summon the narrator.

## What changed in 1.17

**The quest log no longer opens the panel by itself.** On a live realm the quest
log is a pane of the world map, and the panel opened over the very row you had
clicked — so reading a quest's objectives, or abandoning it, meant closing the
panel first. There is a **Word Hunter** button on the log now, and the panel
waits for it. A quest giver's window is unchanged: its text is the reason that
window opened. If you liked the old behaviour, `/whw settings` has a switch for
it, off by default.

**The size sliders are two groups instead of one list.** Text sizes read as the
point size the letters end up at; window sizes read as a percentage of the whole
window. They are different measurements and always were — a font size leaves the
window where you dragged it, and a window size grows the border and buttons too
— so showing both as "80–200%" invited a comparison that could never hold. Your
stored sizes are unchanged; a window you had at 1.2 now says 120%.

## Install

Unzip into `_retail_\Interface\AddOns\`, `_classic_era_\Interface\AddOns\` or
`_forever_\Interface\AddOns\` — the download carries a build for each, then:

1. Set WoW's language and the addon's **Target language** to the same thing — `/whw lang`
2. Open a quest or NPC dialogue, then click the **WordHunterWoW - Reader** book tab
3. Click a word, give it a meaning, save

`/whw` closes whichever of the addon's windows is open — the word list first,
then the statistics, then the quest panel — and opens the quest panel when none
of them is.

## Add a dictionary

You don't have to define every word yourself. A dictionary pack fills them in for you:

| | |
|---|---|
| [German](https://github.com/Ironship/WordHunterWoW-Dictionary-DE) | 104,274 words, every one checked by hand |
| [French](https://github.com/Ironship/WordHunterWoW-Dictionary-FR) | 70,326 words, machine-translated and then read through and corrected by hand (proper names excepted) |
| [Spanish](https://github.com/Ironship/WordHunterWoW-Dictionary-ES) · [Italian](https://github.com/Ironship/WordHunterWoW-Dictionary-IT) · [Portuguese](https://github.com/Ironship/WordHunterWoW-Dictionary-PTBR) | machine-translated, not hand-checked |

The French, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese packs load on demand: QuestWordHunter reads the one for the language you are learning at login, or when you pick it in the settings, so the others cost no memory (each is 24 to 54 MiB once loaded). A pack needs QuestWordHunter 1.22.6 or newer for that — an older one never loads it. The German dictionary also hosts the voice engine and loads with the game.

Want the English quest text side by side? That is [English Quest Panel](https://github.com/Ironship/WordHunterWoW-ENPanel). With it installed, pointing at a German word lights up the English sentence that says the same thing, and picks out the English word itself.

## Helping fill the gaps

Blizzard publishes a quest's title and opening text and nothing else — no objectives, no progress line, no hand-in line, no NPC chatter. Words that live only in those places never make it into a dictionary.

Your game client has them. **Collect quest and NPC text** in `/whw settings` records the passages you actually read, so they can go into the next dictionary release.

It is **off by default**, everything stays on your machine, and nothing is uploaded. Turning it on writes to your own saved data and you decide whether to share it.

```
/whw harvest            what has been collected
/whw harvest on|off     turn it on or off
/whw harvest export     open it in a box you can copy out of
/whw harvest clear      throw it away
```

The recall check has the same shape:

```
/whw recall on|off      ask how well you knew a Learning word before showing its meaning
/whw difficult          how many words are difficult
/whw difficult export   open them in a box you can copy into a flashcard app
```

Supported languages: English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese (Brazil). Retail 12.1, Classic Era 1.15.9 and WoW Forever.

Everything stays on your machine. No uploads.

The settings window's layout is adapted from [DoesItDie](https://github.com/Ironship/DoesItDie) by Joe Greive (MIT).

MIT licence, see [LICENSE](https://github.com/Ironship/WordHunterWoW/blob/main/LICENSE). Issues: [github.com/Ironship/WordHunterWoW](https://github.com/Ironship/WordHunterWoW)

Saving a word keeps its exact position in the current quest: the next shoulder-button press continues to the following word, including repeated words. The editor shows shortcuts inside Save, Cancel, Previous and Next.

Quest-list tooltips open to the left of their quest entry while the WordHunter book tabs or Spoken map panel are visible, keeping the right-side controls clear. Native quest text and controller actions are preserved.

Reader footer shortcuts appear inside Play/Stop, Stats, Words and Copy quest. Defaults while the reader has controller input: left-stick click plays/stops Spoken quest audio, right-stick click opens Stats, X opens Words, and View/Back opens Copy quest. All four actions can be assigned in Key Bindings; explicit WordHunter bindings take priority. The footer grows and wraps to fit the shortcut labels at the selected text size.

Action buttons use Blizzard's red 128RedButton style. Save, Cancel, Previous and Next stand at one height with their captions and shortcuts centred, and the status and footer rows stretch with the editor. Text fields share one flat style, both reader headings use the same typeface, and the scroll-bar arrows no longer reappear on columns that overflow. Words uses pages sized to the visible area: resizing and changing pages reuse the result keys, only the current page resolves word entries, and closing the list releases its results.

Quest history refreshes on demand after quest-log notifications, and side-tab layer scans are throttled while their host is unchanged. Dictionary library data loads only when needed; opening the full quest catalog loads its ranges over several frames. Retail and Forever share these paths.

releases.name: WordHunterWoW 1.22.8
releases.notes:
A performance release for 1.22.7. The word list and the statistics window stop going through the whole German dictionary on every refresh, and logging in and reading a quest with a new word are lighter.

## What's new

- **The word list searches the dictionary quickly.** With the German dictionary, every refresh of the word list (opening it, a status button, the hide-ignored box, each pause in typing in the search box) went through all 143,000 entries: about 0.3 s to list and 0.5 s to search in a run against a stand-in for the game. The first time you open the list after a login or `/reload`, the addon now prepares an index in the background (about 3 s, a few milliseconds a frame). Until it is ready the list works as before; afterwards listing takes about 30 to 60 ms and a search about 10 to 20 ms. The index keeps about 12 MB of memory. The statistics window no longer goes through the dictionary at all.
- **Logging in and reading a quest with a new word are lighter.** The `WordHunterWoWExport` text in your saved variables was rebuilt at every login and each time a quest recorded a new word, about 0.1 s each time. It is now built once, when you log out, so logging out takes about 0.1 s longer.
- **The recall check's controller hints have a row of their own.** With the icons they wrapped onto the scale line and the 1 to 5 buttons.

## State

Checked against a stand-in for the game with real saved variables and the real German dictionary: the old and the new word list give the same lists in 572 comparisons, and the statistics are identical. Not yet tried in the game itself.

## Downloads

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `WordHunterWoW-1.22.8.zip` | the core addon |

Unzip into `World of Warcraft\<game>\Interface\AddOns` (`_retail_`, `_classic_era_` or `_forever_`). The German dictionary and the voice packs are separate downloads.

releases.name: WordHunterWoW 1.22.7
releases.notes:
A fix release for 1.22.6. Controller hints now show the right buttons, and quest audio and word audio can be switched off separately.

## What's new

- **Controller hints match your pad.** On 1.22.6 the hints on buttons, side tabs and in the footer showed the numbered set (1 2 3 4) even where the game's own prompts showed A, B, X and Y. They are now drawn from the same icon set the game's prompts use, so an Xbox pad shows A, B, X, Y, LB and RB. The icons are also larger and easier to read.
- **Enable quest audio.** A new switch under **Settings → Quest panel**, on by default. Turn it off if another add-on, such as Spoken, reads your quests: the narrator window and the Play buttons go away.
- **Enable word audio.** A second switch next to it for the voice that says a German word when you click it. It stays on when quest audio is off. It needs the updated German voice engine (2.0.9) and the word voice pack.

releases.name: WordHunterWoW 1.22.6
releases.notes:
The first stable release since 1.20.0. It brings a new statistics window, one look for every window, keyboard and controller shortcut hints, and load-on-demand dictionaries for French, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese. It runs on Retail, Classic Era and WoW Forever.

## What's new

- **A new statistics window.** Four tabs — Overview, Growth, Forecast and Recall — with figure tiles, your Known words over time and a 30-day pace projection, a forecast of the words that are ready for Known, and your recall ratings.
- **One look for every window.** The windows share the game's own stone and parchment pieces (with a flat fallback on a client that lacks them), and each of the five background styles has its own set. There is a natural and a vivid colour palette, and you can change any of the five text and status colours in **Settings → Appearance**.
- **The other languages' dictionaries load only when needed.** The French, Spanish, Italian and Portuguese packs take 24 to 54 MiB each and were all read at login. Now only the pack for the language you are learning is. They need this version or newer, and they run on Retail, Classic Era and WoW Forever.
- **Shortcut hints on buttons and side tabs.** They use the client's own button names and follow keyboard and controller changes. On Forever they show only in Gamepad Mode. If the client names a pad's face buttons by number, they now read A, B, X and Y instead of 1 to 4.
- **Reading.** The word colours stay readable on the parchment, readable items such as a journal, a letter or a book page open in the same reader as an NPC's conversation, German quest sentences highlight better and show split-verb hints, and with English Quest Panel the English sentence is picked by the words that link the two even when the sentence counts differ.
- **Dictionary words** can be reset to the pack's meaning from the word window.
